workflowRecommendation: Strictly sequential on one branch and one pull request: implement -> test -> review round 1 (COMMENT while the head carries .legion/) -> implementer pushes the .legion/ deletion -> review round 2 (APPROVE naming the clean head by SHA) -> retro (revived implementer, one docs/solutions/ commit) -> merger publishes READY to notifications.role.pr-queue -> merge queue merges -> implementer confirms the file on main and records it on the PR and the Dispatch issue (acceptance 3) -> architect signs off (acceptance 4). The repository has no build, test suite, formatter, or linter; every check is a `legion gh --` command against GitHub whose output is recorded.

implement: legion-worker — supplies the path-limited `jj split`, the `bookmark set -r @- --allow-backwards` push, the PR body READY format with the `Dispatch: LEGSMOKE-154` line, re-run-not-repush for a red check, rebase only on CONFLICTING, the .legion/ deletion push, and the post-merge production check.
legion-retro — the same implementer is revived after the APPROVE for the mandatory retro: one docs/solutions/ commit, one Dispatch issue comment, no handoff write.
dispatch — the retro comment and the post-merge record go on the Dispatch issue with dispatch_comment in plain English; `legion gh` refuses every GitHub-issue write.
test: legion-worker — defines the E2E section the tester fills (real surface, exact command, observation, head SHA, one negative control with links) and the handoff commit/push gate; the negative control here is the shim refusing `pr merge`.
verification-before-completion — each acceptance line is proven by running the named command and recording its output at the head under test; the implementer's handoff is never the evidence.
review: legion-worker — one review per round via `legion gh -- api --method POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/reviews --input` with commit_id; COMMENT while .legion/ is on the head, APPROVE only the clean head named by SHA; CI, threads, and E2E verified on GitHub, never from a handoff; Thermo omitted on this docs-only PR.

concerns: The working-copy commit @ carries the daemon-provisioned, empty .omp/config.yml (snapshot.auto-track = all(); the repository has no .gitignore). It must never reach GitHub. `jj split -m <msg> <paths>` leaves the bookmark on the REMAINDER commit (the new @, which keeps .omp/config.yml and has no description) and `jj bookmark set <name>` without -r targets that same @, after which `jj git push` refuses an undescribed commit. Every phase therefore pushes with `jj bookmark set legion/LEGSMOKE-154 -r @- --allow-backwards` (flag verified present on jj 0.45.1 in this workspace; every prior chain's @origin tip is a described `*: record handoff` commit, confirming the procedure).

Bare `gh` on this pane's PATH is NOT the daemon's worker-bin shim: `which gh` -> /home/ubuntu/.dotfiles/shims/gh, and `gh pr merge 999999 --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke` exits 4 with 'To use GitHub CLI in automation, set the GH_TOKEN environment variable'. The daemon did install /tmp/legion-76-smoke/daemon/worker-bin/gh (100 bytes, execs `legion gh -- "$@"`), but that directory is absent from PATH (PATH starts /tmp/legion-76-smoke/daemon/bin). Every phase runs `legion gh -- ...` explicitly and never bare `gh`; the tester's negative control is `legion gh -- pr merge`, not `gh pr merge`. Reported to the architect as a LEGION-76 rig observation.

Negative-control mechanics verified live from this planner pane: `legion gh -- pr merge 999999 --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --squash` prints exactly 'Legion workers never merge; publish READY to the merge queue' and exits 1; `legion gh -- api --method PUT repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/pulls/999999/merge` prints the same line and exits 1. The guard (isPrMergeInvocation in packages/daemon/src/cli/index.ts) fires before any grant is redeemed or `gh` is spawned, so running it against the real PR number cannot merge or touch GitHub; the tester still confirms the PR state is OPEN afterwards.

The timestamp is chosen ONCE at file creation with `date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ` and appears in both the file name and the single line. The implementer records path, literal, bytes, and sha256 in .legion/implement.json, but the tester and reviewer never trust that: they derive the timestamp from the file name in `pr diff --name-only`, rebuild the literal with the printf template, and cmp the contents-API bytes against it.
Anything written under $LEGION_WORKSPACE is auto-snapshotted into @. Scratch files (PR body, review JSON, expected-bytes file) live under /tmp, never in the workspace.

Both workflows run on `push` AND `pull_request`, so every head shows FOUR check-runs (job `check` x2 from `ci`, job `gate` x2 from `fail-on-demand`), not two — observed on PR #43 head 69d8dd37. `ci` sleeps 20 s; wait with `legion gh -- pr checks <n> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --watch` before reading conclusions. A red run is re-run with `legion gh -- run rerun <run-id> --failed`, never by pushing.

Sibling root LEGSMOKE-153 writes its own marker into smoke/ concurrently (its branch had not been pushed at plan time; locally it carries only .omp/config.yml). Our file name carries `legsmoke154`, so the two cannot collide. main@origin was 40c26543a5fca07a04923de924d2688fce95b0f2 at plan time (one commit past this branch's base 373184959b7a62c7e283f131564b8aeaad9365a2: PR #45 adding smoke/legion16-green-20260913T144851Z.md). A newer main is NOT a rebase trigger — only `mergeable: CONFLICTING` reported by GitHub is (Sami, 2026-09-11).

Byte comparison idiom: `cmp - <(printf ...)` fails on this machine (cmp cannot seek a process substitution; exit 2 'Illegal seek'). Write the expected literal to /tmp/legsmoke154-expected.md with printf and run `... | base64 -d | cmp - /tmp/legsmoke154-expected.md; echo exit=$?`.
Thermo: the PR is one 77-byte markdown file, i.e. docs-only, so per legion-worker the reviewer runs no thermonuclear pass and omits the Thermo line entirely.

After the .legion/ deletion push nothing writes a handoff: cleanup, APPROVE, retro, merger READY, and the post-merge confirmation all report with `legion handoff complete` alone. Recreating .legion/ changes the approved head and restarts the review loop.

The tester and reviewer identities may lack permission to `pr edit` the body (HTTP 403 for a GitHub App that is not the PR author). Fallback: post the exact filled E2E line as a PR comment with the Legion footer and say so in the completion summary so the implementer pastes it into the body on its next push; never leave the evidence only in a handoff.

`legion gh` refuses GitHub-issue writes (`gh issue comment` included); legion-retro's `gh issue comment` example is replaced by dispatch_comment on LEGSMOKE-154, and the acceptance-3 record 'on this issue' is likewise a dispatch_comment.

Rig history: the earlier Legion-chain smoke PRs on this repository (#27, #30, #31, #32, #41, #42, #43) are all still OPEN with zero reviews submitted — every prior chain stalled at the reviewer phase; only tester-driven legion16/green-* probes have ever merged. The review -> cleanup -> APPROVE -> retro -> READY -> merge path this issue must complete has not yet run end to end here; the architect should expect to dispatch the reviewer explicitly after the tester completes.
The repository has no AGENTS.md and no repository-local skills, so the harness skills named in requiredSkills drive every surface.

unchanged -> confirmation only: the tester re-checks the bare gates (four check-runs success at the new head) and edits the E2E head SHA with 'rebase re-check <old> -> <new>: fingerprint unchanged, bare gates only'; a prior APPROVE gets one confirming APPROVE naming both SHAs. changed -> full test round and one new review.

ciFailurePolicy: A failed check-run at any head: read it with `legion gh -- run view <run-id> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --log-failed`. Flaky or infrastructure failure -> `legion gh -- run rerun <run-id> --failed`, never a new commit. Real failure caused by this change (only possible if `.fail-me` reached the tree, which allowedPaths forbids) -> fix in this PR. `ci` cannot fail on content (it only sleeps 20 s and exits 0).
